scope: Find a clean live-spawn recipe for as many of the 25 fully-opaque kinds as possible, before launching a DuckStation session.
method: contact_alloc(x,y,z,ctorType,stackArg) sets rec+0x20 (action_id) directly from metadata table B[ctorType]+0x00 (src_re/contact_alloc_80059e44.c, CONFIRMED field map). Table B (0x8007941C, stride 0x14) is inside the static resident EXE range (0x80010000-0x80082800), so it was read directly, entirely statically, no live session. Scanned ctorType 0..199, built action_id -> [ctorTypes] map, matched against the 25 target kinds.
interpretation: Kinds with a hit can be spawned cleanly via debugger.callFunction on contact_alloc with that literal ctorType -- no post-spawn memory patch needed. Kinds with no hit are NOT reached via contact_alloc's action_id route in this scan range at all; they are very likely type-0x3f PLACEMENT kinds instead (a completely separate spawn path: a placement record's own kind byte, read by the per-frame pickup processor 0x800252a0 -- not contact_alloc). tools/apply_level_placements.py already has a proven, safe 'set_entry' op for this (edit an existing record's kind in place, avoiding the append-corruption bug documented in the pickup-render-kind- descriptor-table memory note). This includes the 22-25 cluster and the 0x1E-typed set (27,37,39,40,47) -- consistent with them being world-placed pickups rather than contact-alloc'd grant/drop objects.
